evals.prompt: Define a typography system in 2-3 sentences. Name its core parts and how components consume it.
expected_elements: Defines it as a rule-governed set of type decisions coherent across surfaces
Names typefaces (display/text/optional mono), a modular size scale, and rhythm rules (line-height, letter-spacing, measure)
Mentions a delivery layer (subset WOFF2, font-display, metrics-matched fallbacks)
States that components consume semantic tokens (display, heading, body, caption), not raw sizes/faces

evals.prompt: Why are type scale steps derived from a single ratio applied to a base size rather than chosen individually?
expected_elements: A single ratio makes sizes reproducible and derivable rather than ad hoc
Produces consistent, perceptible distinction between adjacent levels
Names common ratios (e.g. 1.2, 1.25, 1.333, 1.5) and typical 5-9 steps
Notes too many steps dilute the distinction between adjacent levels

evals.prompt: How are line-height and measure (characters per line) related, and what targets apply to body text?
expected_elements: Line-height and measure are coupled: longer measures need taller line-heights, shorter measures tighter
Body measure target ~45-75 characters per line
Body line-height ~1.4-1.6; display ~1.1-1.3
Letter-spacing tightens at display sizes and positive tracking helps uppercase legibility

evals.prompt: What are the web font delivery best practices for minimizing layout shift and request cost?
expected_elements: Serve WOFF2 and subset to the glyphs/languages actually used
font-display: swap to render fallback immediately
Preload the most-used font files
Metrics-matched fallback @font-face (size-adjust, ascent/descent/line-gap-override) to minimize CLS
Target CLS from font loading below 0.1

evals.prompt: When and why would you use a variable font, and how is it accessed in CSS?
expected_elements: A single file delivers multiple weights/widths/optical sizes via continuous axes (wght, wdth, opsz)
Reduces HTTP requests and makes weight a continuous design decision
Accessed via font-variation-settings or numeric font-weight, not separate files per weight

evals.prompt: A teammate asks the typography-system skill to decide how the H1 should visually dominate the hero section over the subhead and CTA. Is that in scope? Why or why not?
expected_elements: Not in scope — that is visual-hierarchy (deploying type as an ordering signal on a surface)
Typography-system defines the scale and faces that get deployed, not where/how they rank on a given screen
Correctly distinguishes owning the scale/faces/rhythm from owning their per-surface deployment

evals.prompt: A stakeholder says 'a typography system is just picking nice fonts.' Correct the mental model.
expected_elements: Face selection is a small, justified part — not the system
The system (ratio-derived scale, line-height/measure coupling, baseline rhythm, token-mediated delivery) carries hierarchy, brand, and performance
Adding a typeface or hand-picking a size is a cost (bandwidth, hierarchy clarity, cross-OS rendering), not a free aesthetic win

evals.prompt: What would you check to verify a typography system is implemented correctly?
expected_elements: At most three typefaces, each justified by a use the others cannot serve
Scale steps derived from one ratio, not hand-picked
Body measure 45-75 chars verified on rendered lines, not assumed
WOFF2 + subsetting + font-display: swap + metrics-matched fallback; CLS < 0.1
Headings and body share a vertical rhythm snapped to a baseline grid
